intel.t: Main message: electability and personal story. He is a Paralympic gold medalist who won a Trump district, says the race is about having a senator fighting for the people of Iowa, and pitches himself to independents and moderate Republicans.

Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it: attendance. Fox counts 261 missed Iowa House votes from January 12 to May 3, 2026 while he raised money out of state, and the Senate Leadership Fund says he is only showing up for himself. His campaign says Hinson also skipped work for a fundraiser.
Second line of attack: Republicans call him Chuck Schumer's puppet, and Schumer's leadership PAC did give him the maximum.
Strongest coalition: a broad small donor base the campaign puts at nearly 53,000 donors, and a record of winning a Trump district. He outraised Hinson in the second quarter, $2.81M to $2.06M.

Notable recent event: Senate Majority PAC added $17M in fall ads on July 23 on top of a $13.4M reservation. As of August 24 Cook and Fox call the race a toss up, Inside Elections tilts Republican and Sabato leans Hinson.
Cash gap: Hinson held $6,749,491 to his $2,362,314 on June 30, 2026.

bottom: Turek is a small donor candidate carried by national Democratic outside money. He raised $6,276,527 through June 30, 2026 and outraised Ashley Hinson in the second quarter, $2,813,428 to $2,059,828, but held $2,362,314 in cash against her $6,749,491, per Little Village on July 17, 2026, https://littlevillagemag.com/turek-democrats-outraise-republicans/.
Three interests combine real money with a decision he would touch:

**National Democratic leadership.** Senate Majority PAC reserved $13.4 million in May and added $17 million on July 23, 2026. Chuck Schumer's leadership PAC gave him the maximum. The decision is which party organizes the Senate in January 2027.
**VoteVets.** Its super PAC spent about $10 million to win him the June 2 primary, more than both campaigns combined. He says he wants dark money out of politics.

intel.t: Main message: Trump endorsed Republican running on taxes, veterans and costs, with One Nation ads on ending the estate tax and her own ads attacking Turek since June.

Biggest vulnerability as opponents frame it: personal enrichment. Senate Majority PAC says her net worth grew by $8M in Washington and that she backed a tax break for her family business; Democrats say she kept private insurance agency stock. Her campaign calls it a shameless lie.
Second vulnerability: health costs and Medicaid after her vote for the 2025 law, the core of more than $30M in Democratic reservations.
Strongest coalition: party infrastructure and cash. She had $6,749,491 on June 30 and the NRSC committed $29M. Iowa has about an 8 point Republican registration edge and Trump won it by 13 in 2024.

Notable recent event: Bleeding Heartland reported on August 24 that Republicans seem increasingly worried, with Cook calling the race a toss up; she has since called the Iran war a political liability.
Pipeline exposure: Rastetter and Summit's CEO hosted an August 5 fundraiser for her while 78 percent of Iowans opposed eminent domain for pipelines in a 2023 poll.

bottom: Hinson is the party's candidate with the cash. She raised $10,262,866 through June 30, 2026 and held $6,749,491, nearly three times Josh Turek's cash, per Little Village on July 17, 2026, https://littlevillagemag.com/turek-democrats-outraise-republicans/. The NRSC committed $29 million to help her and One Nation planned $11 million.
Four interests combine money with a decision she would touch:
**Senate Republican leadership.** The NRSC, the Senate Leadership Fund and One Nation carry her air war. The decision is the Senate majority in January 2027.

**Agribusiness and the carbon pipeline.** Bruce Rastetter, founder of Summit Agricultural Group, gives and raises for her. Summit's pipeline is the most unpopular project in Iowa farm politics, and she has no public position on it in sources read.

D.t: Josh Turek leads by 2.4 in the forecast and wins 65% of simulations. The cushion is about 33,318 votes; a one point swing is about 6,856 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +4.1 and D +9.6. A normal polling error decides it.
The polls page average is D +1.9. Your best recent poll is Marist College at D +5.7; your worst is CNN/SSRS at R +3.0. 22 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Polk, a projected net 54,389 votes; Johnson, a projected net 31,029 votes; Linn, a projected net 21,756 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Dallas, D +4.6, 3.6% of the vote; Dubuque, D +7.8, 3.2% of the vote; Pottawattamie, D +2.4, 2.6% of the vote; Woodbury, D +1.9, 2.5% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Josh Turek runs furthest behind in Johnson, Dallas, Sioux. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 92% of voters, 49 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.62 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 72% of voters, 50 to 48, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.62 points; Voters without a degree, 65% of voters, 51 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.23 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Josh Turek: Immigration voters 21 to 77, Small counties 41 to 56, Voters who can afford daily costs 44 to 54. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$2.4M cash against $6.9M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
Registered Democrats cast 47% of the 407,374 ballots in Iowa so far, against 34% for the other party. That is 10.4 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 2.0 points away from Josh Turek. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
